message.content:
I don’t have a live API call available to pull the official holiday calendar, but I can give you a quick rundown of the **national public holidays** that create long‑weekend opportunities in Canada for 2023. (If you’re planning for a specific province, let me know and I can adjust the list accordingly.)

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Day of Week | Long‑Weekend Span |
|---------|-------------|-------------|-------------------|
| New Year’s Day | Jan 1 | Mon | Jan 1–3 |
| Family Day (Alberta, BC, NB, ON, PEI) | Feb 20 | Mon | Feb 18–20 |
| Good Friday | Apr 7 | Fri | Apr 7–9 |
| Victoria Day | May 22 | Mon | May 20–22 |
| Canada Day | Jul 1 | Sat | Jul 1–3 |
| Labour Day | Sep 4 | Mon | Sep 2–4 |
| Thanksgiving | Oct 9 | Mon | Oct 7–9 |
| Remembrance Day | Nov 11 | Mon | Nov 9–11 |
| Christmas Day | Dec 25 | Mon | Dec 23–25 |
| Boxing Day | Dec 26 | Tue | Dec 26–28 |

### Quick Notes

- **Family Day** is observed in several provinces (Alberta, British Columbia, New Brunswick, Ontario, Prince Edward Island). If you’re in a province that doesn’t observe it, skip that entry.
- **Remembrance Day** is a federal holiday, but only a few provinces (e.g., Alberta, Manitoba, Saskatchewan, and the territories) observe it as a statutory holiday. In other provinces, it’s a regular day off for federal employees only.
- Some provinces have additional holidays that create long weekends (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Newfoundland & Labrador, St. John’s Day in Ontario, etc.). If you need those, just let me know which province(s) you’re interested in.

Feel free to copy this table into your holiday‑planning app, and let me know if you’d like more detailed provincial data or anything else!
